accessibility:
Tabs built from `Tabs.Tab` follow the [WAI-ARIA tabs pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/), with manual activation.

| Key                 | Action                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Enter the tab list on the selected tab, or leave it from whichever tab has focus                |
| `→` / `←`           | Move focus to the next / previous tab, wrapping at either end                                   |
| `↓` / `↑`           | Move focus to the next / previous tab in a `vertical` tab list (`→` and `←` keep working there) |
| `Home` / `End`      | Move focus to the first / last tab                                                              |
| `Enter` / `Space`   | Activate the focused tab: select it, show its panel and call `onChange`                         |

- The tab list is a single tab stop. While focus is in it, the stop follows focus, and once focus leaves it returns to the selected tab.
- Activation is manual: moving focus with the arrow keys, `Home` or `End` doesn't change the panel or call `onChange`. `Enter`, `Space` and a click do. A key press activates the tab through a click on it, so click listeners see keyboard activation too.
- The arrow keys, `Home` and `End` skip disabled tabs. A disabled tab is marked `aria-disabled` and never takes the tab stop. When the selected tab is disabled, or no tab matches `value`, the enabled tab with the lowest `index` takes it, so the list can still be reached.
- `Tabs.List` is the `tablist` (marked `aria-orientation="vertical"` in a `vertical` layout), each `Tabs.Tab` is a `tab` with `aria-selected`, and each `Tabs.Content.Item` is a `tabpanel`. A tab names its panel in `aria-controls` and a panel names its tab in `aria-labelledby`, so the panel is announced with the tab's label. The ids are generated, and when you pass your own `id` to a tab or a panel, the other side follows it.
- Panels aren't focusable themselves. When a panel holds nothing focusable, pass it `tabIndex={0}` so `Tab` moves from the tab list into it.
- The focus ring shows for keyboard focus only, drawn inside the tab in Bulma's focus color, width and style (`--bulma-focus-h`, `--bulma-focus-s`, `--bulma-focus-l`, `--bulma-focus-width`, `--bulma-focus-style`). In a `toggle` row, a focused tab comes in front of the neighbors that overlap it, so none of them covers the ring's edge. A disabled tab is dimmed, with a not-allowed cursor and no hover. All of this comes from the bestax extras (`extras.css`, or `bestax.css`, which includes them), the same styles that show and hide the panels.
- **Forced colors:** Bulma marks the active tab with colors alone, which forced colors (Windows' contrast themes) replaces, so bestax's styles draw a bar in the system's highlight color along the bottom of the active tab there, in every style, in a `vertical` layout and for a link in an active `Tabs.Item`. The tab and everything in it stay in the contrast theme's colors, and a disabled tab is drawn at full strength in the theme's color for something disabled, rather than dimmed. This comes from the bestax extras too.
- On a right-to-left page a `vertical` layout mirrors: `side="left"` puts the tabs at the right, where the line starts, and `side="right"` at the left. The line between the tabs and the panel, and the selected tab's mark on it, stay on the side that faces the panel.
- Built from `Tabs.Item`s with links inside, as in most examples above, the tabs are Bulma navigation, and the keys, roles and disabled look above don't apply. Give each link an `href`, so a keyboard reaches it and a screen reader offers it as a link, and put `aria-current="page"` on the current tab's link: `active` adds only Bulma's `is-active` class, which shows the current tab but doesn't announce it. Hold the items in a plain `<ul>` rather than `Tabs.List`, which marks its list as a tab list for `Tabs.Tab`. Each link is its own tab stop and keeps the browser's link behavior and Bulma's focus ring, in Bulma's focus color, width and style. For a link placed directly in the `Tabs.Item`, the bestax extras draw that ring inside the link, where the tab row would otherwise clip its top and bottom, and bring a focused `toggle` tab in front of the neighbors that overlap it. A selected `toggle` tab keeps the ring where Bulma draws it, so the row still clips its top and bottom there, except in forced colors, where it's drawn inside as well. The forced-colors bar applies to these tabs too.
- Use clear text or icons with labels for each tab, and provide `aria-label` or screen-reader text for icon-only tabs.
summary: The `Tabs` component provides flexible and fully-featured Bulma tab navigation for your Bulma React UI. Built from `Tabs.Tab`, the tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with manual activation: the tab list is a single tab stop, the arrow keys, Home and End move focus between tabs (skipping disabled ones), and Enter or Space activates the focused tab. Each tab names its `Tabs.Content.Item` in `aria-controls`, and each panel names its tab in `aria-labelledby`. Built from `Tabs.Item` with links inside, the tabs stay plain Bulma navigation.

Built from `Tabs.Tab`, the tabs follow the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with manual activation: the tab list is a single tab stop, the arrow keys, Home and End move focus between tabs (skipping disabled ones), and Enter or Space activates the focused tab. Each tab names its `Tabs.Content.Item` in `aria-controls`, and each panel names its tab in `aria-labelledby`. Built from `Tabs.Item` with links inside, the tabs stay plain Bulma navigation.

props.name: isFullwidth
props.description: Tabs expand to fill the horizontal space.

props.name: isFullWidth
props.description: Tabs expand to fill the horizontal space.
props.deprecationNote: Use `isFullwidth` instead — `isFullwidth` wins if both are set.

props.name: fullwidth
props.description: Tabs expand to fill the horizontal space.
props.deprecationNote: Use `isFullwidth` instead — `isFullwidth` wins if both are set.

props.name: rounded
props.description: Tabs use the rounded toggle style (only with `toggle`).

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color for tab underlines and active state (renders `is-<color>`). Bulma ships no tabs color CSS, so this prop has never had a visual effect for any value. Passing it logs a console warning in development.
props.deprecationNote: No `.tabs.is-<color>` CSS exists; the prop renders unstyled and will be removed in the next major version.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback when active tab changes. Called with the tab's `index` when a `Tabs.Tab` is activated: clicked, or Enter or Space pressed on it. Moving focus with the arrow keys, Home or End does not call it, because activation is manual: focus moves freely and the selected tab changes only when the user picks one.

props.name: vertical
props.description: Renders tabs vertically. With a `Tabs.Content`, the tab list is also marked `aria-orientation="vertical"` and ArrowUp and ArrowDown move focus between tabs, alongside ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (the layout stacks horizontally on mobile).

props.name: side
props.description: Side placement when `vertical` is true. The row follows the page's direction, so on a right-to-left page `left` puts the tabs at the right, where the line starts, and `right` puts them at the left.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Makes tabs take up the full width equally.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: The `<ul role="tablist">` that holds the `Tabs.Tab`s. Navigation built from `Tabs.Item`s goes in a plain `<ul>` instead.

Individual tab button. Consumes Tabs context for active state management. Renders `<a>` internally — consumers provide only the label text/children. Inside a `Tabs` it takes part in the tab list's keyboard support and links to the `Tabs.Content.Item` with the same `index`.

props.name: index
props.description: Tab index for matching with content.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the tab. A disabled tab is marked `aria-disabled`, cannot be activated, is skipped by the arrow keys, Home and End, and never holds the tab list's tab stop. The bestax extras styles also dim it and turn off its hover.

extraProps.name: id
extraProps.description: The tab's id, which its panel names in `aria-labelledby`. Generated inside a `Tabs` when omitted; a passed `id` is used and the panel follows it.

extraProps.name: onKeyDown
extraProps.description: Called before the tab handles the key; call `event.preventDefault()` to stop the tab handling it.

parts.summary: A navigation tab: an `<li>` holding a link of your own, with an `href`. Put the items in a plain `<ul>`, and mark the current one with `active` and its link with `aria-current="page"`. For tabs that switch what's shown in place, use `Tabs.Tab` with `Tabs.Content`, which handle the selection and the keyboard.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the tab as the current one with Bulma's `is-active` class, and nothing else: no ARIA attribute says so. Put `aria-current="page"` on the link inside the current tab, so a screen reader announces it.

parts.summary: Container for tab content panels. No custom props beyond `children` and standard `<div>` HTML attributes. Applies the `.tabs-content` class.
Individual content panel. Shows/hides based on active tab from context.

props.name: index
props.description: Tab index for matching with content.

extraProps.name: id
extraProps.description: The panel's id, which its tab names in `aria-controls`. Generated inside a `Tabs` when omitted; a passed `id` is used and the tab follows it.

extraProps.name: tabIndex
extraProps.description: The panel is not focusable by default. Pass `0` when it holds nothing focusable, so Tab moves from the tab list into it.
